result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers argue against enforcing first, treat the copies as a symptom of a slow board, and give a similar ordered plan. A is slightly ahead because it offers to bless one-off changes as marked exceptions instead of setting migration deadlines. It is also more open about what it can't tell, stating its assumptions, noting that request-age and fork numbers have to come from the board and repos, and naming capacity as the real constraint. Neither answer says outright what to stop doing or how requesters can see request status. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reject enforcement as the first move, treat the forks as a sign of unmet needs, and give similar ordered plans of triage, a response SLA, a fork audit and light guardrails. B handles the forks better because it allows a fork to stay as a marked exception instead of only setting a migration deadline. B is also clearer about what it can't know: it names its assumptions, says which metrics to pull from the board and repos, and asks whether two people can clear the backlog. It comes closer to naming something to stop doing, by moving from building every request to reviewing contributions.
